content: 1. Any user with an account can opt to receive notifications about changes to specific pages by using the watch feature and managing their watchlist. 2. MediaWiki does not allow users to own pages, but the watchlist feature, combined with the ability to revert changes, enables users to stay engaged with specific pages without granting them full control over the content. 3. When logged in, users can find a watch or unwatch link on the margin of each non-dynamically generated page. Clicking this link adds or removes the page and its corresponding talk page (or vice versa) to or from the user's watchlist. 4. Changes to the watchlist apply to both the main page and its associated talk page; it is not possible to watch one without the other. 5. When saving an edited page, the Watch this page checkbox determines whether the page will be added to the watchlist. 6. If the user preference Add pages you edit to your watchlist is enabled, the checkbox will be automatically selected, and the page will be added to the watchlist unless the checkbox is manually deselected before saving. 7. Users can manage their watchlist, including mass unwatching of pages, by using the Watchlist &magic=yes feature, accessible via a link at the top of the watchlist. 8. The watchlist provides a customized recent changes view, showing only the pages the user is watching. 9. The watchlist displays watched pages in reverse chronological order based on the time of the last edit, with optional cutoff times. 10. Enhanced watchlists show details of the last edit (or multiple edits), including the date, time, type of edit (minor or major), a link to the page, the difference between versions, the page history, the editor's username, and the edit summary. 11. By default, the watchlist also shows the change in bytes (+/-) since the last version. 12. Minor changes cannot be excluded from the watchlist. 13. In the non-enhanced watchlist, only the last edit to a page is shown, and there is no indication of whether major changes occurred recently if the last edit was minor. 14. To view all changes since the last check, users must review the page history. 15. Moving a watched page does not appear on the watchlist, but both the old and new page names remain watched after the move. 16. The watchlist is just one feature for monitoring pages; specifying pages to watch is useful even without actively using the watchlist. 17. In Recent Changes, Enhanced Recent Changes, and Related Changes, watched pages are bolded, and the message updated (since my last visit) appears for changes. 18. To reset the notification flag, users must be logged in when viewing the page. 19. Depending on user preferences, email notifications can be sent when a watched page is edited by someone else. However, further notifications will not be sent until the user views the page. 20. Email notifications can optionally ignore minor changes. 21. New features are being developed to address the potential overload of email notifications, such as delayed emails summarizing multiple edits or specifying subsets of watched pages for email notifications. 22. Watching pages detects changes in the wikitext only, not changes in the rendered page. 23. Users can also watch templates and nested templates to monitor changes indirectly affecting the rendered page. 24. Watching an image page or category page is limited to changes in the editable part of the page. 25. It is not possible to watch an image or a category in the sense of being notified when pages are added or removed. 26. Users can watch non-existing pages, which will appear on their watchlist when someone creates them. 27. Deletion of a watched page does not appear on the watchlist, but deleted pages can be identified using Watchlist &magic=yes, which lists all watched non-talk pages, including deleted ones. 28. Talk pages are not listed separately, so the deletion of a talk page cannot be detected in this manner. 29. The Related Changes feature can be used to create watchlist-like functionality by linking to specific pages or subpages. 30. Unlike the standard watchlist, Related Changes does not automatically include talk pages, so links to talk pages must be added manually. 31. Watching a category or image does not notify users of additions or removals of pages from the category or changes to the image itself. 32. Users can define custom CSS styles to highlight links to selected pages, allowing for extra emphasis or differentiation based on categories of interest. 33. Watchlist privacy is maintained, as ordinary users and administrators cannot see the contents of another user's watchlist or who is watching a particular page. 34. Developers with access to the servers hosting the database can access this information, but public database dumps do not include it.
